To measure the effect of inter-shot consistency on expected standing points, we simulate 10,000 goalie seasons, all with seasonal save percentages of .900, by sampling seasonal shot outcomes without replacement into a sequence (or, a season). Then, we calculate the [entropy](/2022/03/28/goalie-consistency-1.html) of each simulation, along with the expected standing points earned. The results are below.

![Expected standing points by simulated inter-shot goalie consistency.](/figs/goalie-two-one.png){fig-alt="Expected standing points by simulated inter-shot goalie consistency." width="60%"}

*Inter-shot consistency does not seem have an effect on expected standing points.*

The [next post](/2022/04/07/goalie-consistency-4.html) will use entropy as a measure for goalie consistency on real data. It will be a similar exploration to [this one](https://github.com/namitanandakumar/Draft-Analysis/blob/master/Streakiness/VanHAC%202018.pdf) on shooters, except it will be expanded to include weights on shots in the form of [MoneyPuck](https://moneypuck.com/)’s Expected Goals.
